subject: 5-Bullet Friday — Tick Warfare, Insane Rock Climbing, Bizarre Meditations, and More

bullets.title: World’s Hardest Flash - Adam Ondra Climbs 5.15 (9a+) First Try
bullets.note:
)**.”**
I’m finally getting back into basic rock climbing after elbow surgery, and I
love it. I’m watching tutorials to progress from V3/V4 to higher grades, but I
also love mini-docs about beyond-insane feats of athleticism. This one is
worth watching, even if you’ll never touch a climbing wall.
**
**[Adam
Ondra](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/wnh2hghqel9v8lc7hx/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9hZGFtLm9uZHJhLw==),
the Czech phenom widely considered the best rock climber alive, sets out to do
something no human had ever done: climb a 5.15a route on his very first try,
without having laid hands on the rock. This video tracks it and has guest
appearances from [Alex
Honnold](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/reh8hohmgo9vnpc2h6/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE2LzA1LzE3L2FsZXgtaG9ubm9sZC8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1jb252ZXJ0a2l0JnV0bV9tZWRpdW09Y29udmVydGtpdCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249NWJm),
[Chris
Sharma](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/08hwh9h23p0wq8clh5/aHR0cHM6Ly9lbi53aWtpcGVkaWEub3JnL3dpa2kvQ2hyaXNfU2hhcm1h),
and others.

The preparation ritual alone is worth the price of admission: coached by
former World Champion [Patxi
Usobiaga](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/8ghqhohom7epwehkh9/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9wYXR4aXVzb2JpYWdhX3B1Y3Nlcmllcy8=),
he visualizes every single move from the ground, twitching through the
sequence like he’s downloading it into his nervous system. It’s a masterclass
in mental rehearsal that applies far beyond climbing. The footage comes from
the [Reel
Rock](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/vqh3hrhozq23mxughl/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9yZWVscm9jay8=)
team—directed by Peter Mortimer of [Sender
Films](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/l2hehmhl8d5vqni6h0/aHR0cHM6Ly9zZW5kZXJmaWxtcy5jb20v),
Josh Lowell of [Big UP
Productions](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/m2h7h5h3dlk029hmhq/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9iaWd1cGNsaW1iaW5nLw==),
and Zachary Barr—the crew behind many of the most popular climbing films of
the last two decades.

If you want to take that inspiration into the gym, pair it with “[BIGGEST
MISTAKES Coach Louis Sees at Every Grade
(V0–V9+)](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/dpheh0hel2zwdwfmh4/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj1oNU94cDlxdWplRQ==)”
from [Hannah Morris
Bouldering](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/e0hph7h78d9wm2t8h2/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vQEhhbm5haE1vcnJpc0JvdWxkZXJpbmc=),
featuring coach [Louis
Parkinson](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/7qh7h8h9rxvpd4hzh6/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9jYXB0YWluY3V0bG9vc2Uv)
of [Catalyst
Climbing](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/owhkhqhw203lx4avhr/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY2F0YWx5c3RjbGltYmluZy5jb20v)—one
of the clearest breakdowns I’ve seen of common errors. It was immediately
helpful to me.

bullets.section: What I’m adding to my coffee while traveling
bullets.title: MCT Oil Powder
bullets.note:
)**.**
I only add MCT oil powder to coffee while fasted. These days, that means
drinking it well before my first meal around 2–3pm. Here’s why I used MCT oil
at all:

MCTs are readily converted into ketones, which the brain can use as an
alternative fuel source. [One study in people with Alzheimer’s
disease](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/e0hph7h78d9wm5i8h2/aHR0cHM6Ly9wdWJtZWQubmNiaS5ubG0ubmloLmdvdi8yOTkxNDAzNS8=)
found that MCT supplementation doubled the brain’s consumption of ketones, and
[a six-month randomized trial in people with mild cognitive
impairment](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/7qh7h8h9rxvpddazh6/aHR0cHM6Ly9wdWJtZWQubmNiaS5ubG0ubmloLmdvdi8zMzEwMzgxOS8=)
found improvements in several measures of cognition. That said, the evidence
is still mixed, and [a 2024 systematic
review](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/owhkhqhw203lxpcvhr/aHR0cHM6Ly9wdWJtZWQubmNiaS5ubG0ubmloLmdvdi8zODcxNTcwNS8=)
concluded that current evidence is insufficient to recommend MCTs as a
treatment for Alzheimer’s or mild cognitive impairment. Personally, I cycle on
and off of MCT (and any exogenous ketones) for weeks at a time, and when I’m
on-cycle, I only consume the equivalent of 1–2 tablespoons of liquid MCT each
morning, 3–4x per week. Warning: high potential for disaster pants if you’re
not accustomed to MCT + caffeine, so best to be near a bathroom.

To further explore this topic, listen to my podcast episodes with [Dr. Tommy
Wood](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/z2hghnheqm9r56cph0/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDI2LzAxLzI4L2RyLXRvbW15LXdvb2QtaG93LXRvLWZ1dHVyZS1wcm9vZi15b3VyLWJyYWluLWZyb20tZGVtZW50aWEtdHJhbnNjcmlwdC8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1jb252ZXJ0a2l0JnV0bV9tZWRpdW09Y29udmVydGtpdCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249NWJm)
and [Dr. Dominic
D’Agostino](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/p8heh9h4npk5roiqh3/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDI2LzAxLzA2L2tldG9zaXMtcHJhY3RpY2FsLWd1aWRlLWRvbS1kYWdvc3Rpbm8vP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9Y29udmVydGtpdCZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTViZg==).

bullets.title: We’re Living in a Tick Nightmare. It’s Time to Go to War.
bullets.note:
)**”**(_The
New York Times_) [Alternate
link](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/6qheh8hlm3v6x8hohk/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcmNoaXZlLmlzLzJRVXh6).
This is a sobering piece on why tick-borne disease is exploding across the
Eastern U.S. and why the author thinks we should treat it the way we once
treated malaria: as a public problem with a public solution, not a personal
one solved by tucking your pants into your socks. It also gets into alpha-gal
syndrome (AGS), the tick-borne red-meat/mammalian-product allergy, which can
be fatal. This is something I’ve seen in my family, and I myself have had Lyme
disease twice from growing up on Long Island.**

**Here is an excerpt that could be from a horror movie:
**
** _The lone star tick, especially, seems as if it crawled out of a horror
flick. With its aggressive approach to hunting and unusually long, barbed
mouthparts designed to anchor into our flesh, it resembles a miniature version
of the alien in the ‘Predator’ movies. Unlike most other ticks, which take a
let’s-see-what-comes-along approach, the lone star will pursue you for several
yards. It’s fast, able to crawl up a leg in seconds and is one of the
relatively few tick species whose larvae bite humans: Step on a cluster of
lone star babies and you will soon find hundreds of poppy-seed-size vampires
coating your ankle. They can even push through your socks._**

**Another excerpt—with a statistic difficult to fathom in 2026:

 _**In the 1930s, malaria afflicted 30 percent of the people living in the
Southeastern United States.**_****_The government undertook an ambitious
campaign to fight it, and in less than a decade, public health workers dug
thousands of miles of ditches, drained half a million acres of swampy mosquito
breeding grounds and sprayed four million homes with insecticides.

It worked. Death rates from malaria plummeted, and the disease was eliminated
from the country by 1951. As Rachel Carson documented in her 1962 book,
“Silent Spring,” that effort led to its own cascading ecological and health
crises: mosquitoes developed resistance to the insecticide DDT, which also had
disastrous effects on wildlife and proved toxic to humans._*** **Question for
scientists or others in the know:**

If we treated ticks as we have treated malaria-carrying mosquitoes—in an all-
out war of eradication—what might it look like if we wanted to minimize
collateral damage and avoid novel chemicals?

Does anyone out there have good technologies or approaches that might scale?

Please let me know by tagging me with [@tferriss on
X](https://click.fourhourmail.com/k0udre388b6h5od9dwflho8oo7kmb8h08x/kkhmh6hnkog2zkilh7/aHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS90ZmVycmlzcw==),
including a #ticks hashtag, so I can find you.

bullets.title: “A writer—and, I believe, generally all persons—must think that whatever happens to him or her is a resource. All things have been given to us for a purpose, and an artist must feel this more intensely. All that happens to us, including our humiliations, our misfortunes, our embarrassments, all is given to us as raw material, as clay, so that we may shape our art.” — Jorge Luis Borges
